destination.title: Scalar potentials, field geometry and gravitational EFT consistency
destination.question: How are scalar potentials and field excursions constructed, compared and constrained in gravitational effective theories, and what follows conditionally for their physical applications?
destination.summary: This is a proposed navigational family. The packet supplies numerical membership but no original intensional region definition to certify. Most candidates have an identifiable potential, field-geometry or EFT-validity target; several peripheral candidates have only methodological overlap or an unestablished connection.

systems: Scalar effective theories coupled to gravity
targets: Field normalization, distance and EFT breakdown
Controlled potential construction and numerical diagnostics
regimes: Positive and negative potentials, distinguished explicitly
Local stationary points and finite-distance evolution
assumptions: Each conjecture is a proposed restriction or adopted conditional premise
Control, dimensionality and dynamical assumptions remain source-specific
conventions: Full gradient norms, directional slopes and trajectory derivatives are distinguished
Source-specific potential definitions and normalization conventions are retained
includes: Ordinary and pre-Swampland construction or computational work
Counterexamples, unresolved extensions and premise checks
Negative-potential contraction and scalar interaction bounds as distinct branches
excludes: An established universal exclusion of de Sitter configurations
Automatic identification of every numerical candidate with the scalar-potential core
Fine-question equivalence inferred from broad-card membership

sources.title: The string swampland constraints require multi-field inflation

evidence.text: Are the proposed criteria valid throughout the string landscape? The source leaves this open and identifies realized KKLT-like de Sitter constructions as a possible failure of the positive-potential gradient restriction.

sources.title: Bounds on Slow Roll and the de Sitter Swampland

evidence.text: Can increasing the number of light fields generate hierarchically small slow-roll parameters or evade a Planck-unit field-range restriction? A separate unresolved question concerns weakening a tachyon bound with the number of negative eigenvalues.

sources.title: Draining the Swampland

evidence.text: Can a scalar effective theory describe particle physics and cosmology while satisfying a positive lower bound on its total potential gradient and a restricted field-space range?

sources.title: Quantum Corrections and the de Sitter Swampland Conjecture

evidence.text: Which statements about a potential gradient follow from comparing nearby scalar configurations?

sources.title: The Landscape, the Swampland and the Era of Precision Cosmology

evidence.text: Does consistency with string quantum gravity exclude metastable positive-energy vacua, or require an order-one potential gradient throughout positive-potential field space?

sources.title: Uplifting Runaways

evidence.text: Can a warped potential with small value and absolute slope still have a sufficiently large metric-normalized relative slope to satisfy the conjectured de Sitter criterion?

sources.title: Distance and de Sitter Conjectures on the Swampland

evidence.text: Which restrictions on scalar potentials follow in limits where string theory admits parametrically controlled observables? The limits include weak string coupling and other infinite-distance directions, with distances and Hessian eigenvalues measured using the scalar kinetic metric.

sources.title: Distance and de Sitter Conjectures on the Swampland

evidence.text: Can a positive axion maximum violate the original gradient conjecture while satisfying the refined Hessian branch? The answer depends on the canonical decay constant and precise potential, including any offsets or additional harmonics.

sources.title: The Asymptotic dS Swampland Conjecture ‐ a Simplified Derivation and a Potential Loophole

evidence.text: Does quantum gravity require an order-one logarithmic slope for positive potentials near infinite field distance, subject to the refined conjecture's curvature qualification?

sources.title: Spinodal solution to swampland inflationary constraints

evidence.text: Which dynamical and perturbative assumptions turn a potential-slope bound into a tensor lower bound? This reconstruction isolates the potential-driven, canonical slow-roll baseline challenged by the paper.

sources.title: Further refining the de Sitter swampland conjecture

evidence.text: Do positive minima in particle-physics or reheating descriptions provide admissible quantum-gravity counterexamples, and how should thermal contributions enter the potential criterion?

sources.title: Compact objects and the swampland

evidence.text: The model provides self-gravitating scalar configurations on which to test conjectural field-range and potential-slope bounds. Equal-mass real scalars form a complex field with a radial, positive mass-plus-quartic potential.

sources.title: Eternal Inflation and the Refined Swampland Conjecture

evidence.text: Can a stationary maximum have sufficiently small classical drift for diffusion while retaining the negative curvature required by the refined conjecture? A local quadratic hilltop separates these two requirements.

sources.title: A brief remark on convexity of effective potentials and de Sitter Swampland conjectures

evidence.text: Do de Sitter conjectures exclude familiar phenomenological scalar potentials? The note names the perturbative Standard Model Higgs and QCD axion potentials and asks whether using the full convex potential changes the apparent conflict.

sources.title: Thermodynamic interpretation of the de Sitter swampland conjecture

evidence.text: Can thermodynamics constrain metastable de Sitter local minima when no increasing-species downhill direction exists? The paper leaves this question open, including its application to the cited KKLT and large-volume scenarios.

sources.title: Eternal Inflation in Swampy Landscapes

evidence.text: Which conjectural restrictions on scalar potentials obstruct de Sitter vacua, slow roll, or hilltop quantum diffusion?

sources.title: Trans-Planckian Censorship and the Swampland

evidence.text: What curvature restriction follows for a quadratic hilltop over a specified fractional drop in positive potential? The setting fixes the maximum V0, constant negative curvature, and endpoint potential c_qV0.

sources.title: String Gases and the Swampland

evidence.text: Does a slope calculation for a gas-induced moduli energy test a conjecture formulated for bare scalar potentials?

sources.title: Fundamental Physics, the Swampland of Effective Field Theory and Early Universe Cosmology

evidence.text: How do the potential slope and field excursion needed by simple Einstein-scalar cosmologies compare with the conjectural effective-field-theory restrictions reviewed next?

sources.title: de Sitter Conjectures in $N$=1 Supergravity

evidence.text: Can a supergravity construction produce positive rolling energy with an exponential slope small enough for the phenomenological bound quoted in the paper?

sources.title: Notes on quantum corrections of swampland and trans-Planckian censorship conjectures

evidence.text: The reviewed conjectures ask whether a quantum-gravity-compatible effective theory can support a sufficiently flat positive potential or a long period of inflation. A small gradient does not by itself evade the refined conjecture because a negative Hessian eigenvalue is an alternative branch.

sources.title: Strengthening the de Sitter swampland conjecture in warm inflation

evidence.text: Which field excursions and scalar potentials can belong to an effective theory compatible with the conjectured quantum-gravity constraints?

sources.title: The Effective Potential Originating from Swampland and the Non-trivial Brans-Dicke Coupling

evidence.text: How does the paper interpret decreasing potentials and potentials with local minima under the invoked de Sitter Swampland conjecture?

sources.title: Higuchi Bound on Slow Roll Inflation and the Swampland

evidence.text: Does the upper-gradient restriction survive outside the bimetric slow-roll approximation as a general unitarity constraint? Can a concrete string compactification satisfy the combined gradient conditions with controlled approximations?

sources.title: KKLT and the Swampland Conjectures

evidence.text: Can an α′-corrected nonperturbative potential supply a saddle approaching the logarithmically extended TCC duration bound?

sources.title: Non-canonical kinetic structures in the swampland

evidence.text: Can a similar geometric construction constrain scalar theories with explicit higher derivatives? This remains open for galileon and Horndeski models; the paper does not claim its P(φ,X) construction automatically extends to them.

sources.title: Non-canonical kinetic structures in the swampland

evidence.text: Can a conjectured restriction on sigma-model potentials constrain scalar actions with nonquadratic derivative dependence? The paper asks this for P(φ,X), where X = −(∂φ)²/2, and introduces an auxiliary-field extension to apply the geometric criterion.

sources.title: Supercritical String Cosmology drains the Swampland

evidence.text: Which scalar potentials can belong to a critical-string low-energy theory admitting a quantum gravity completion? The reviewed conjectures constrain scalar displacement, potential slope, or negative curvature near a maximum.

sources.title: Testing Swampland Conjectures with Machine Learning

evidence.text: Are the sampled critical points compatible with the Refined dS conjecture when compared through critical-point potential values and the smallest Hessian eigenvalue? The supplied paragraph only initiates this diagnostic.

sources.title: Axion monodromy inflation, trapping mechanisms and the swampland

evidence.text: Which scalar trajectories satisfy the adopted quantum-gravity conjectures? The paper imposes an order-one excursion limit and a slope-or-negative-curvature condition, using the slope branch to test inflation on a positive linear potential.

sources.title: The string swampland constraints require multi-field inflation

evidence.text: Construct a unit velocity vector using the kinetic metric, differentiate it covariantly, and project the equation of motion onto the resulting tangent and normal. The operation applies to an on-shell multi-scalar trajectory without requiring a two-dimensional target space.

sources.title: Bounds on Slow Roll and the de Sitter Swampland

evidence.text: Replace explicit critical-point field values by potential energies, solve the resulting linear constraints, and optimize the normalized smallest Hessian eigenvalue subject to signs. The procedure yields sufficient instability bounds without finding individual vacua, provided the scaling truncation and scalar normalization are valid.

sources.title: Draining the Swampland

evidence.text: Add a scalar sector and jointly test retained-field status, energy, metric gradient, curvature, field range and evolution. The operation does not infer consistency from a large isolated-sector logarithmic slope.

sources.title: Quantum Corrections and the de Sitter Swampland Conjecture

evidence.text: Specify the kinetic metric, compute the directional derivative, apply the dual-norm inequality, and divide by the displacement norm. This transfers a premise rather than generating a universal positive constant.

sources.title: The Landscape, the Swampland and the Era of Precision Cosmology

evidence.text: Fit observations directly in the physical model's parameter space with Bayesian MCMC, and independently profile the likelihood for the reported single-exponential check. This retains model information omitted by the envelope comparison.

sources.title: Uplifting Runaways

evidence.text: Evaluate tension and RR-charge contributions, substitute the warped background, and minimize radial placement. Since I(T) decreases, the anti-D3 energy is minimized at the tip.

sources.title: A potential mechanism for inflation from swampland conjectures

evidence.text: Which potential should carry a quantum-gravity gradient bound when a modulus interacts with additional sectors?

sources.title: Warm inflation as a way out of the swampland

evidence.text: Can a simple steep monomial potential become compatible with the assumed bounds and observations through dissipation? The benchmark isolates this question without claiming global compatibility of the potential around its minimum.

sources.title: Relating the scalar weak gravity conjecture and the swampland distance conjecture for an accelerating universe

evidence.text: Can exponentially light towers at large scalar-field distance, together with an entropy bound on an accelerating causal patch, constrain scalar self-interactions relative to gravity?

sources.title: Higgs potential near-criticality from a de Sitter swampland-like condition

evidence.text: How can positive late-time energy coexist with the exact-potential restriction? The paper considers a metastable perturbative vacuum and a rolling scalar configuration.

sources.title: Distance and de Sitter Conjectures on the Swampland

evidence.text: Could a potential-gradient bound follow from a scalar weak-gravity restriction on an extended object whose tension equals the potential? The paper proposes this correspondence as a future research direction.

sources.title: An Alliance in the Tripartite Conflict over Moduli Space

evidence.text: Which fields must be integrated out to obtain the bubble-constrained slow-motion theory, and does its scaling distance remain finite, become logarithmic, or have another behavior?

sources.title: Constraints on field flows of quintessence dark energy

evidence.text: Is a nearly flat positive scalar potential compatible with an order-one lower gradient bound proposed for ultraviolet-completable gravity?

sources.title: Rigid nongeometric orientifolds and the swampland

evidence.text: Can quantum gravity permit positive potentials with small gradients and no sufficiently unstable Hessian direction?

sources.title: Relating the scalar weak gravity conjecture and the swampland distance conjecture for an accelerating universe

evidence.text: Could microscopic light-tower multiplicities constrain scalar potentials through an entire hierarchy of derivative inequalities?

sources.title: Is the trans-Planckian censorship a swampland conjecture?

evidence.text: Do ordinary scalar potentials contain positive stationary configurations that defeat universal censorship? Higgs, meson, and axion examples connect this question to particle physics.

sources.title: The zoo plot meets the swampland: mutual (in)consistency of single-field inflation, string conjectures, and cosmological data

evidence.text: Can positive potential curvature cancel part of the gradient contribution to the scalar tilt while remaining compatible with tensor limits?

sources.title: Landskepticism or why effective potentials don't count string models

evidence.text: Can extrema of string-derived effective potentials establish a landscape of quantum-gravity models, and what cosmological definition and probability measure would make its predictions meaningful?

sources.title: f(R) and Brans-Dicke Theories and the Swampland

evidence.text: How does Jordan-frame matter modify the scalaron potential relevant to the adopted Einstein-frame gradient test?

sources.title: The web of swampland conjectures and the TCC bound

evidence.text: Can quantum-gravity consistency constrain the slope of a positive scalar potential? The reviewed TCC formulation assigns a specific dimension-dependent coefficient to an asymptotic exponential bound.

sources.title: From Swampland to Phenomenology and Back

evidence.text: Do familiar low-energy scalar potentials contain positive-energy stationary points incompatible with the original de Sitter proposal? The paper uses the Higgs potential and a conditional axion potential as examples.

sources.title: Draining the Swampland

evidence.text: Does the positive-gradient conjecture allow the familiar isolated potential description of spontaneous symmetry breaking?

sources.title: On the origin and fate of our universe

evidence.text: What restrictions do string theory and Swampland principles place on positive scalar potentials, and what conditional consequences follow for inflation, dark-energy stability and the future of our universe?

sources.title: De Sitter Space and the Swampland

evidence.text: Can an averaged null-energy inequality replace pointwise NEC in an argument constraining the gradient of a lower-dimensional scalar potential?

sources.title: The Asymptotic dS Swampland Conjecture ‐ a Simplified Derivation and a Potential Loophole

evidence.text: Can the tower-limited effective theory resolve the curvature generated by a positive potential? The necessary comparison is between its ultraviolet cutoff and the potential-defined scale H.

sources.title: Further refining the de Sitter swampland conjecture

evidence.text: Can one covariant inequality constrain the potential gradient and instability together while excluding positive minima and allowing small slow-roll parameters in suitable regions?

sources.title: Bumping into the Species Scale with the Scalar Potential

evidence.text: Can a positive string-derived scalar potential reproduce the species scale's qualitative descent from a bulk maximum toward zero, including a bump in its logarithmic gradient rate, and what generates that bump?

sources.title: Trans-Planckian Censorship and the Swampland

evidence.text: How long may the constructed scalar configuration persist under the earlier constraint invoked by the paper? The appendix compares its residence time with H⁻¹ ln(1/H).

sources.title: Contracting cosmologies and the swampland

evidence.text: Can a negative scalar potential from string theory remain sufficiently steep over the field interval required for slow contraction? The paper distinguishes compatibility with a lower slope bound from the harder task of constructing an actual ekpyrotic potential.

sources.title: Primordial Gravitational Waves and the Swampland

evidence.text: The two-scalar model tests how a heavy field's displacement changes a light-field potential over a large excursion. The coupling makes the light mass depend on the heavy field's expectation value.

sources.title: Dimensional reduction and (Anti) de Sitter bounds

evidence.text: Which positive-potential gradient bounds retain their form under classical dimensional reduction?

sources.title: Further refining the de Sitter swampland conjecture

evidence.text: How can scalar potentials coupled to gravity be compared using quantities independent of field coordinates? The paper uses the gradient norm and minimum covariant Hessian eigenvalue to diagnose positive extrema, potential instability, and potential slow roll.

sources.title: Higgs Inflation and the Refined dS Conjecture

evidence.text: Why does adding a negative-curvature alternative change the phenomenological implications of the original gradient conjecture? The reviewed examples are positive stationary potentials, the electroweak Higgs potential, quintessence, and slow-roll inflation.

sources.title: Single versus multifield scalar potentials from string theory

evidence.text: How common are genuinely single-field string effective theories, and can positive potentials obey a universal asymptotic lower bound on a single directional slope? Does restricting to physical trajectories change the answer?

sources.title: From Swampland to Phenomenology and Back

evidence.text: The scalar-sector setting asks whether the total potential of a low-energy theory is compatible with conjectured gravitational consistency conditions. Canonical normalization and inclusion of all scalar directions are essential when comparing slopes and Hessian eigenvalues.

sources.title: Local random potentials of high differentiability to model the Landscape

evidence.text: How can random potentials be generated locally in a chosen differentiability class C^k, retaining GOE Hessian statistics while avoiding finite-step Hessian jumps that obstruct cosmological perturbation calculations and searches for minima?

sources.title: Machine Learning and cosmographic reconstructions of quintessence and the Swampland conjectures

evidence.text: Do reconstructed late-time field excursions and positive-potential slopes fall within the conjectured ranges associated with effective theories compatible with quantum gravity?

sources.title: The dS swampland conjecture with the electroweak symmetry and QCD chiral symmetry breaking

evidence.text: Can a scalar stabilized today develop a large pion-induced gradient and weaken the bound on the original de Sitter conjecture?

sources.title: Two‐Field Axion Inflation and the Swampland Constraint in the Flux‐Scaling Scenario

evidence.text: Can a positive potential satisfy the proposed quantum-gravity gradient condition while its cosmological trajectory inflates?

sources.title: A Strong Scalar Weak Gravity Conjecture and Some Implications

evidence.text: What inconsistency follows from violating the scalar bound, how do formal extremal solutions become physical states, and how should the criterion extend to interacting scalars or other dimensions?

sources.title: Hyperbolic field space and swampland conjecture for DBI scalar

evidence.text: What replaces canonical field distance and potential derivatives for a nonlinear scalar Lagrangian P(X,ϕ)? Normalizing the small-X expansion, temporal perturbations, or spatial perturbations produces different candidates away from slow roll.

sources.title: de Sitter in non-supersymmetric string theories: no-go theorems and brane-worlds

evidence.text: Can membrane weak gravity enforce a slope bound after restoring contributions not generated by the membrane?

sources.title: The Convex Hull Swampland Distance Conjecture and Bounds on Non-geodesics

evidence.text: Does a scalar no-force condition determine the minimum exponential rate required by the SDC?

sources.title: Higuchi Bound on Slow Roll Inflation and the Swampland

evidence.text: Does positivity of the scalar helicity kinetic term of a massive spin-two field on FLRW impose an upper limit on a slowly rolling scalar-potential gradient? The paper investigates this question using nonlinear bimetric gravity.

sources.title: A brief remark on convexity of effective potentials and de Sitter Swampland conjectures

evidence.text: Which scalar potentials can describe low-energy physics in theories admitting a quantum-gravity completion? The comparison uses canonical scalar derivatives, minimal gravitational coupling, and the reduced Planck mass M_p.

sources.title: Compact objects and the swampland

evidence.text: How far may a scalar move while a low-energy theory coupled to gravity remains valid? The conjectural rationale is that large target-space distances produce an exponentially light tower that invalidates the truncated effective action.

sources.title: Relating the scalar weak gravity conjecture and the swampland distance conjecture for an accelerating universe

evidence.text: How strongly do the original and revised scalar interaction inequalities constrain positive potentials approaching an inflationary plateau?

sources.title: Contracting cosmologies and the swampland

evidence.text: How do quantum-gravity consistency arguments constrain a negative scalar potential during homogeneous contraction? The application assumes a canonical scalar minimally coupled to Einstein gravity and dominating a flat FLRW universe, with negative time approaching a crunch at zero.

sources.title: The entropic quasi-de Sitter instability time from the distance conjecture

evidence.text: Can a positive-potential stationary point remain approximately de Sitter when its slope vanishes, or must negative normalized curvature produce an instability?

sources.title: Warm Inflation in the light of Swampland Criteria

evidence.text: How far can a scalar move while a low-energy effective description remains valid? The paper adopts an order-unity excursion limit motivated by exponentially light states at large field-space distance.

sources.title: Bounds on Slow Roll at the Boundary of the Landscape

evidence.text: Can a positive stationary point with vanishing first and second derivatives still admit an order-one potential drop within an order-one field distance?

sources.title: Moduli-dependent KK towers and the swampland distance conjecture on the quintic Calabi-Yau manifold

evidence.text: Does the effective slope change with distance, or does a different branch supply the asymptotically lightest state?

sources.title: The $F$-term Problem and other Challenges of Stringy Quintessence

evidence.text: Can present acceleration arise from thermal trapping at positive energy even when the underlying zero-temperature potential obeys a de Sitter restriction?

sources.title: Small-Field and Scale-Free: Inflation and Ekpyrosis at their Extremes

evidence.text: Does quantum gravity obstruct steep negative potentials needed for small-field ekpyrotic scaling, and can counterexamples or cosmologies satisfying all proposed restrictions be constructed?

sources.title: Asymptotic accelerated expansion in string theory and the Swampland

evidence.text: Can string-theoretic runaway potentials support asymptotic accelerated expansion at parametric control, particularly when several potential terms compete rather than one dominating?

sources.title: Phenomenological Consequences of the Refined Swampland Conjecture

evidence.text: Can a proposed quantum-gravity restriction on scalar-potential slopes or negative curvature produce useful low-energy constraints? The paper uses particle potentials and inflationary observations to test the allowed sizes of the conjecture coefficients c and c′.

sources.title: Lorentz-Violating Inflation and the Swampland

evidence.text: The baseline asks whether a single scalar in conventional GR can sustain slow roll and the paper's target of 60–70 e-folds while obeying two proposed quantum-gravity bounds.

sources.title: De Sitter Space and the Swampland

evidence.text: How should scalar-potential steepness be compared independently of the choice of field coordinates?

sources.title: Power Law Plateau Inflation Potential In The RS $II$ Braneworld Evading Swampland Conjecture

evidence.text: Can a potential with an order-one normalized gradient still drive slow-roll expansion when the expansion law differs from ordinary four-dimensional cosmology?

sources.title: Type I Hilltop Inflation and the Refined Swampland Criteria

evidence.text: Can increased cosmological friction permit slow evolution on a potential with order-one negative curvature? The brane formulas separate the dynamical slow-roll parameters from the normalized potential derivatives constrained by the refined conjecture.

sources.title: Draining the Swampland

evidence.text: Can a supergravity scalar sector generate logarithmic functional behavior for a proposed drainon?

sources.title: Draining the Swampland

evidence.text: If the gradient conjecture obstructs potential slow roll, do negative-potential or fast-roll cosmological alternatives avoid that particular condition?

sources.title: Higgs potential near-criticality from a de Sitter swampland-like condition

evidence.text: What changes when the de Sitter gradient restriction acts on the exact quantum effective potential? The paper investigates this choice and its phenomenological consequences.

sources.title: Gravitational Wave Signatures from Warm Dark Energy

evidence.text: Can gauge-induced friction sustain late-time axion slow roll on a potential whose slope satisfies the quantum-gravity conjectures considered by the paper?

sources.title: Jumping Through Loops: On Soft Terms from Large Volume Compactifications

evidence.text: Can one bulk divisor become exponentially larger than another while physical cycles remain controlled and the scalar potential stabilizes both directions?

sources.title: On finite time singularities in scalar field dark energy models based in the RS-II Braneworld

evidence.text: The conjecture supplies a proposed quantum-gravity restriction on scalar potentials. The paper asks whether enforcing this slope bound changes the existence or character of singularities in its RS-II dark-energy system.

sources.title: Bounds on Slow Roll at the Boundary of the Landscape

evidence.text: Can the nonlocal scalar-potential bound be derived from a higher-dimensional energy condition? The paper nominates ANEC and relative-entropy monotonicity as possible ingredients but leaves their connection to compactification bounds unresolved.

sources.title: Gauss–Bonnet Inflation and the String Swampland

evidence.text: Can a positive potential satisfying |V′|/V ≥ c produce small tensor power without invalidating the assumed slow-roll expansion?

sources.title: Quantum Breaking Bound on de Sitter and Swampland

evidence.text: Which positive scalar potentials permit a Hubble patch to leave an approximately de Sitter phase before its proposed quantum break-time? The paper studies unstable extrema and slow roll away from extrema.

sources.title: A note on Inflation and the Swampland

evidence.text: Can an apparently nonflat potential become a plateau when its scalar kinetic term is canonically normalized? The example combines a quadratic potential with a double pole in the kinetic coefficient.

sources.title: De Sitter Space and the Swampland

evidence.text: Can a quantum-gravity scalar potential have an arbitrarily small positive-energy slope?

sources.title: Negative scalar potentials and the swampland: an Anti-Trans-Planckian Censorship Conjecture

evidence.text: Can restrictions on blueshifting modes in contracting universes characterize negative scalar potentials compatible with quantum gravity, including their asymptotic slopes and possible implications for AdS scalar masses?

sources.title: The Swampland Spectrum Conjecture in Inflation

evidence.text: Does a scalar potential change the field-space distance relevant to the appearance of light quantum-gravity states? The proposed answer uses the length of a trajectory lifted to the potential graph.

sources.title: Dark Energy in String Theory

evidence.text: Which leading single-modulus supergravity potentials can have positive energy and a sufficiently small saxion slope without balancing several unrelated contributions?

sources.title: Thermodynamic interpretation of the de Sitter swampland conjecture

evidence.text: Which part of a proposed restriction on positive scalar potentials follows from entropy and temperature, and which part requires rapid growth of light species along a modulus direction?

sources.title: Higgs potential near-criticality from a de Sitter swampland-like condition

evidence.text: Can a scalar effective theory admit positive-energy stationary configurations while satisfying proposed quantum-gravity restrictions? The original gradient condition forbids them; the refined alternative permits sufficiently unstable positive-energy configurations.

sources.title: Racetrack Potentials and the de Sitter Swampland Conjectures

evidence.text: Can extra contributions or axionic tuning flatten a positive racetrack saddle enough to challenge the refined curvature bound?

sources.title: de Sitter Extrema and the Swampland

evidence.text: Could a restriction involving both slope and curvature accommodate unstable classical extrema while still constraining positive-potential scalar theories?

sources.title: Bounds on Slow Roll at the Boundary of the Landscape

evidence.text: What can the shape of a positive multifield potential constrain without specifying cosmological initial conditions? The paper studies gradient, tachyon and finite-distance descent diagnostics, with lengths measured using the scalar kinetic metric.
